links.reason: Fragment 1 (யானையொ(டு) அரும்கலம் துறுத்துப் பணிந்துவழி மொழிதல்) and Akananuru 124 (நன்கலம் களிற்றொடு ... வணங்கினர், வழிமொழிந்து) share the tribute formula of jewels, elephants and submissive speech. The akam poem applies it as the condition (என்ப ஆயின்) of the soldier's homecoming, so the cross-genre use is real and the teaches sentence says what the pair shows.

Both use a tree in its seed: Sivavakkiyar's ஆலவித்தில் ஆல்ஒடுங்கி is an image of Parabrahman within, while Neelakesi 776 (வித்தினு ளுண்டென ... நீள்பனை) mocks the Sankhya claim that the effect pre-exists in its cause. These are different subjects, mystic indwelling and causal theory, so the shared image is real but the incompatibility is thin. The Siddhar's point is not a claim about causation, so the other-side gain (an objection it never answers) overstates the case.

759 makes space one and running through உலகு and அலோகம்; 295 asks whether the room of souls and matter (மன்னுயிர்க்கும் புற்கலக்கும் இடன்) would not pass every bound of the world without dharma and adharma. Together they give the Jain reason the world's limit cannot come from space. The note and teaches are accurate.

Aputhiran's release sets a condition: ஓர் யாண்டு ஒரு நாள் தோன்று ... அருள் அறம் பூண்டு ஆங்கு ஆர் உயிர் ஓம்புநர் உளர்எனில் அவர் கைப் புகுவாய். 11:57-58 has the bowl enter Manimekalai's hand (செங் கையில் ... பாத்திரம் புகுதலும்) as she circles Gomukhi. A condition and its fulfilment is a sound within-epic develops, and the verdict on her compassion follows from the Tamil.

243 charges the one who gave himself and his wives (தன்னை யீந்ததும் தாரங்க ளீந்தது) and took that as dharma; in 398 the narrator tags the Buddhist speaker பெண்டானம் ஈயும் அறங்கொண்ட பெருமையினான். The narration takes up the debater's charge, as the teaches sentence says, though one recurrence hardly makes it a 'standing' epithet.

Mokkalan's dilemma (ஒன்றெனின் ... பிறபிற வாயின பிறபொருளாம் ... ஒன்றுரை) concerns substance and quality. The Manimekalai's ஒற்றுமை நயம் and வேற்றுமை நயம் concern cause and effect (காரண காரியம் ஆகிய பொருள்களை). The contrast between a demand for one answer and two allowed viewpoints is real, but it holds across different pairs, so the tension is thin.

The blessing has தொல்லை வினையால் துயருழந்தாள் beside கண்ணின்நீர் கொல்ல உயிர் கொடுத்த கோவேந்தன் வாழியரோ, and so keeps both of the patikam's causes (அறம்கூற்று ஆவதூஉம், ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும்) while praising the king who paid. The note's 'the king dharma killed' is loose, since the Tamil says her tears killed him, but the qualification is real.

The units connect: 3:1-3 has heavenly women freed from a curse at the தலைக்கோல் தானத்து, and 6:20-24 has a dancer cursed to earth (மண்மிசைத் தங்குக இவள்எனச் சாபம்) from whose line Madhavi comes. The teaches sentence says Madhavi's first performance was 'said to end' the curse, but 3:1-7 only compares or links her birth to the freed women (பிறப்பிற் குன்றா); it does not say her debut ends a curse.

Kovalan reports தீதுதீர் மதுரையும் தென்னவன் கொற்றமும், set in a city praised for கோலின் செம்மை; the king later says யானோ அரசன் யானே கள்வன் ... என்முதற் பிழைத்தது. The claim and the scene that refutes it are linked in the way the brief allows for within-epic links, and the victim's praise as the measure of the king's self-sentence is specific.

Neelakesi 208 says no living person asks for flesh, eyes or head (வாழு மாந்த ருழைவரு வாரில்லை). Purananuru 43 praises the ancestor who entered the scales for a dove (தபுதி யஞ்சிச் சீரை புக்க வரையா ஈகை). But the dove story is protection of a refugee from a hawk that did ask for flesh, so the 'test of need' does not touch it squarely. 'Tamil tradition did not hold it as a settled virtue' overreaches from one polemic verse.

97 names கொன்ற பாவம் and ஊன் தின்ற பாவம் separately in hell; 163 opens the debate with ஊன்றின்றல் இழுக்கென்னான். The sermon's separate sin of eating grounds the first charge, a doctrinal set-up and its use across chapters, not plot sequence.

Kural 388 says the just protector is இறையென்று வைக்கப் படும்; Senguttuvan says birth into a protecting line is துன்ப மல்லது தொழுதக வில். One speaks of how the people regard the just king, the other of how the office feels from inside, in fear of rain failing and of a life wronged. That is a limit on the honour, not an opposite judgment of the same thing, and the gains clause itself states it as the view from inside.

Naladiyar 195 (நல்ல குலமென்றும் தீய குலமென்றும் சொல்லள வல்லால் பொருளில்லை) states the principle, and Aputtiran argues it from inside the brahmins' own lore with ஆன் மகன் அசலன் ... ஆவொடு வந்த அழி குலம் உண்டோ நான்மறை மாக்காள் நல் நூல் அகத்து. The contrast between an outside standard and a charge of inconsistency is accurate, and both gains hold.

27:57-77 lists eight பிரமாண ஆபாசங்கள், errors of cognition, and 29:450-472 closes the Buddhist account of அனுமான ஆபாசம், faults in a stated proof. These are different topics in a sequence of lessons, not two catalogues dividing one ground. Ending on inference does not show that the Buddhist teacher 'locates falsehood' in arguments rather than cognitions, so the qualification is a contrast of subject dressed up as more.

Kannaki's vow is conditional (பட்டாங் கியானுமோர் பத்தினியே யாமாகில் ஒட்டே னரசோ டொழிப்பேன் மதுரையும்), and the housewives who keep the household dharma (வருவிருந் தோம்பி மனையற முட்டாப் பெருமனைக் கிழத்தியர்) answer it with கொங்கைப் பூசல் கொடிதோ அன்றென and worship of the fire. That is a vow and its answer, and the teaches sentence is specific.

The materialist dismisses knowledge of former birth as தெய்வ மயக்கினும் கனா உறு திறத்தினும் மையல் உறுவார் மனம் வேறு ஆம் வகை ஐயம். In Silappathikaram 30 the knowing god appears on the Brahmin woman (இம் மறையோ டன்மேற் றோன்றி) and the hidden births return before the court (ஒளித்த பிறப்புவந் துற்றதை). The note gives the sceptic's view as the materialist's, not the work's, and the conflict is a defensible one; strictly the god possesses the Brahmin woman and the girls recall through the water.

Against the materialist's escape (தெய்வ மயக்கு, கனா), Neelakesi 874 offers the newborn who runs to the breast (தாய்முலை யோடல்) as something the five elements just joined cannot do (ஐந்து பூதமுஞ் செறிந்த நாள்களுட் செய்வன வல்ல). The pairing shows why the Jain picks evidence that cannot be called a delusion, though the verse itself does not name former birth.

The shared word is real: the fleeing kings become ஆடு கூத்தர் (26:228), and Maadalan's soul is ஆடுங் கூத்தர்போல் ... கூடிய கோலத் தொருங்குநின் றியலாது (28:165-166). But the teaches sentence's 'mocked by the king's rivals' and 'recoils on the mocker' are not in either unit: no one in these lines mocks the disguised kings in a way the sermon turns back.

445 defines the Lord's greatness by அட்டக வித்து வெந்தாம், and 458 says வித்தென்றும் வெந்தால் முளையல ... பிறப்பின்றிச் சித்தி யகத்து ... நித்திய மாகி. One image does two jobs, defining lordship and showing that release is not extinction, as the teaches sentence says.

Both units have an elephant tamed: Kovalan frees the Brahmin from the rogue elephant and is hailed கருணை மறவ, and Udayakumaran subdues the musth elephant (கடுங்கண் யானையின் கடாத் திறம் அடக்கி). But in 4:27-46 the taming serves no desire: it quells a rampage through Puhar before he hears of Manimekalai. So 'serving desire the second time' is not in the Tamil, and the father-daughter frame is the proposer's addition.

Neelakesi cites உண்டியா லுடம்புளதாலுடம்பினா லுணர்வாம் as common knowledge, and Tirumular says உடம்பார் அழியில் உயிரார் அழிவர் ... மெய்ஞ்ஞானஞ் சேரவு மாட்டார் and so nurtures the body. The premise is shared and the uses differ. But Neelakesi's use does not limit Tirumular's case; it is a different conclusion in a different quarrel, so the other-side gain is not true, and 282 lines 3-4 are uncertain.

Silappathikaram 21:42 has கோநகர் சீறினேன் குற்றமிலேன் யான், and Manimekalai 26:34-37 has சீற்றம் கொண்டு செழு நகர் சிதைத்தேன் ... அடு சினப் பாவம் எவ் வகையானும் எய்துதல் ஒழியாது. The same act is judged faultless and sinful in Kannaki's own voice, a real tension, and the teaches sentence names what it turns on.

Neelakesi 138 hails the sage who வெல்லற் கரிய வனங்கனைமெய் வெண்ணீ றாக வெகுண்டோய், and Pattinattar's verse names the Lord who opened his fire-eye to burn Kama (காமனைக்கண்ணாலெரிக்கக்கனல்விழித்த). It is a shared figure, the burning of Kama. That the Jain hymn is 'a borrowing ... pointed against' the Saiva text, and that a much later Siddhar verse is 'contested' by it, is not shown by either verse.

The Puhar warriors offer their heads so that the offering may be a bulwark of the king (பலிக்கொடை புரிந்தோர் வலிக்குவரம்பு ஆகவென), without judgment; Champapathi answers உலக மன்னவர்க்கு உயிர்க்கு உயிர் ஈவோர் இலரோ இந்த ஈமப் புறங்காட்டு அரசர்க்கு அமைந்தன ஆயிரம் கோட்டம். On the plainer reading the note names, the second epic denies what the first epic's rite assumes, in the same city.

The epic names திருமா வளவன, and Purananuru 66 addresses கரிகால் வளவ. The link joins them as one king by the shared Valavan name alone, which the brief rules forced. The epic also does not 'remove every human limit': it says only that he found no foes (பொருநரைப் பெறாஅ) and that the mountain stopped him, so the claimed loss of the Sangam check is the proposer's construction.

Paripadal 5:9 names the hill only as குருகொடு பெயர் பெற்ற மால் வரை, and Thiruppugazh 38 has நெட்டைக் க்ரவுஞ்சம் பிளந்து with the sea dried. The observation that one renders the name in Tamil and the other borrows it is true and specific. But nothing is developed: the pair is a shared deed and figure, so same_image fits better.

Kural 911 is conditional on women who அன்பின் விழையார் பொருள்விழையும். Kovalan finds Madhavi தன்றீ திலள் and the fault his own (என்தீ தென்றே). The epic shows a courtesan outside the couplet's class rather than a case the rule 'cannot explain', so there is no incompatible claim. The gains clause that Kovalan clears her against a 'rule it overturns' is not true; the pair is a limit, not a tension.

158 has கூறு வேனெனக் கூறாய் குரன்முர சனையதோர் குணத்தை, speech without the will to speak, and 682 turns the Ajivika's argument (அறிந்தா னறிந்தன தான்சொல்லின் ஆர்வச் சினத்தனனாய்) that a knower who speaks falls into longing and anger. Reading the hymn's paradox as the answer to that dilemma is apt and specific.

Nanmanikkadigai 80 has கொடுப்பின் அசனங் கொடுக்க, and Kural 226 has அற்றார் அழிபசி தீர்த்தல் அஃதொருவன் பெற்றான் பொருள்வைப் புழி. They agree that food for the hungry is the best use of wealth. Joining 'best gift' to 'safest store' adds little beyond the shared claim, and nothing in the quatrain develops the couplet.

The verbal tie is real: உடம்பொடு முயிரிடை (64:1) and the couplet's உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு. But 64 is an epithet of the sage, who knows the scripture that cuts the deeds bound up in the ஒற்றுமை வேற்றுமை of body and soul, set in a scene where he sees through the disguise; and its reading is uncertain. The contrast with the couplet's bird leaving the nest is fair but thin.
links.text_issue: line 3 (பணிந்தவரட் காசிடை) is obscure; the verse number is reconstructed (printed as 6)

links.reason: The link turns on கடுவினையேன் as 'the woman of cruel deeds' who owns the burning. In வல்வினைவந் துருத்தகாலைக் கணவனையங்கு இழந்துபோந்த கடுவினையேன் the word reads at least as naturally as 'I, of harsh fate', the one the strong deed struck. The claim that she 'keeps the burning as her own act' and 'does not hide behind' fate stretches one word.

Kavunthi's saying (வானம் பொய்யாது ... நீணில வேந்தர் கொற்றம் சிதையாது பத்தினிப் பெண்டிர் இருந்தநா டென்னும் அத்தகு நல்லுரை) and her இத்தெய்வம் do extend the wife's power from rain to the king's victory beside Kural 55. But the teaches sentence's claim that the couplet 'keeps the wife below the gods' is not in தெய்வம் தொழாஅள் கொழுநன் தொழுதெழுவாள், which sets her apart from worshipping gods, not beneath them.

The burning-ground bones are shared in the words: the Naladiyar's புறங்காட் டுதிர்ந்துக்க பல்லென்பு and the Neelakesi's புன்றோலும் பல்லென்பும் போர்த்த புறங்காட்டு ளன்றே யுறைவன். Both refuse the praise of beauty, the quatrain from having seen, the sage from living there. The memory and way-of-life contrast and both gains hold.

203 says a power passing across is either a sixth beside the five (ஐந்தன்றிப் ... ஆறாகாவோ) or முழுக்கேடு; 580 says the lac is something beyond the seed but nothing is shown beyond the five (வியலகத் தைந்திற்கும் வேறொன்று காட்டாய்). It is the same dilemma against disciple and teacher, and teaches rightly states it as Neelakesi's case.

The scene does repeat the possessive words: the kings say எமது ஈது and cannot let go of their பெரும் பற்று, and the sage says இருஞ் செரு ஒழிமின் எமது ஈது. But Kural 350 bids the seeker hold the attachment of the one who has none (பற்றுக பற்றற்றான் பற்றினை). The kings are not shown taking up the sage's attachment; he silences their claim with his own. Saying the couplet's paradox is 'staged' needs a generous reading.

Kundalakesi 19 has a steadfast man who says பாரித்த தெல்லாம் வினையின்பயன், and Neelakesi 184 says the Buddhists themselves (நுமர்) hold துன்பந்தான் றீவினையின் வழித்தோன்றும். On that tenet the two agree; the fragment makes no claim about the Buddha suffering for others, so it is not in tension with the Neelakesi. What the pair gives is a Buddhist attestation of the premise Neelakesi turns.
links.text_issue: Kundalakesi 19 is a fragment whose man and plot are unnamed

links.reason: Manimekalai 30:212-213 gives சித்தம் உற்பவித்தது மின்போல் as an example of இல்லது சார்ந்த உண்மை வழக்கு, a mode of speech, and Neelakesi 196 attacks the mind that perishes wholly with what it knew (அறக்கெட்டிங் கெள்ளனைத்து மில்லென்றால் இறப்பறித லெவனாகும்). The opposition over the momentary mind is real, but it rests on one example in a list of speech modes, so the link is thin.

The verbal parallel is real: கடவுட் பத்தினிக் கற்கால் கொண்டபின் ... கங்கைப் பேர்யாற்றுக் கரையகம் against கடவுள் பத்தினிக் கற்கோள் வேண்டி ... கங்கை மண்ணி. But the teaches sentence and the epic-side gain assume that the Patitruppattu preface is an earlier, independent Chera witness that 'already' called her a goddess. Nothing in the two texts fixes that order, and the preface may depend on the epic.

6:66-67 does repeat 3:14-15 (பதினோர் ஆடலும் பாட்டும் ... விதிமாண் கொள்கையின் விளங்க). But in 3:12-15 the formula describes what the dance master knows, not Madhavi's training as the note says. In 6:46-67 the vidyadhara tells his beloved to see the gods' dances (காணாய்) without naming Madhavi as the performer, so the curriculum-to-performance reading needs help from outside the units.

313 rejects the Buddhist rule that sin joins only by intention (சென்று சேர்தலைச் சித்தம தின்மையால்), and 595 argues that wherever there is mind there is action (எங்குச் சித்தமுண் டவ்வழிச் செய்கையு முண்டே). These run in different directions: one says sin attaches without intention, the other that intention implies action. The claim that the meat-eater quarrel 'rests on' 595's thesis is not shown.

The teaches sentence says 'the order of the three aims differs by book', but both ends are the Kural. The tension is also doubtful: 760's wealth is ஒண்பொருள், bright or rightly gained wealth, which is compatible with 39's அறத்தான் வருவதே இன்பம்.

59 has her take Kamalekai's form (காம லேகைதன் னுருவொடு திருவெனத் தோன்றி), and 134 has her shed it (மாய வுருவ மாறித்தன்மற்றை யுருவ மேகொண்டு) and confess as பேயேன். The later verse reverses the earlier, and the teaches point that conversion begins with ending the deception and naming her nature is specific.

claims.gist: the ten perfections are giving, morality, patience, energy, meditation, wisdom, skill in means and the rest

claims.gist: of the three remedies, right knowledge is to know without defect the realities beginning with the soul
